warning: Do not read an oracle before completing all three run modes for that fault. Oracle review is adjudication, not a debugging hint.

oracles.truth: loadOrderWorkspace awaits three requests in sequence in the plain service module.
oracles.acceptedDiagnosis: The three request starts are serialized by explicit awaits; investigate whether customer/pricing dependencies are truly sequential.
oracles.honestyRequirement: Invocation/common-caller attribution may identify the service callsite; it does not prove that parallelization is semantically safe.
oracles.verificationExpectation: Manual or finding-guided network timing/count comparison can be useful; causality must not be upgraded from before/after timing alone.

oracles.truth: Two requests race; the newer fast result updates state first and an older slower completion later overwrites it.
oracles.acceptedDiagnosis: The stale completion wins last because the component does not guard request identity/order before setResult.
oracles.honestyRequirement: Network timing alone is not proof of the state-write/business cause. Level 0 should stay source/causality-limited rather than inventing a root cause.
oracles.verificationExpectation: A meaningful verification requires an explicit UI/state target or targeted operation evidence; unsupported automation is acceptable.

oracles.truth: After a large report response, HeavyReport sorts rows and intentionally burns the main thread for about 135 ms.
oracles.acceptedDiagnosis: Synchronous post-fetch processing blocks the main thread; investigate reducing, chunking, or moving CPU-heavy work.
oracles.honestyRequirement: A worker opportunity is a recommendation, not proof that a worker is the correct business fix.
oracles.verificationExpectation: A before/after duration target is useful only if the compared workflow isolates the same report work.

oracles.truth: VueFaultLabComponentErrorProbe throws from its render path after the controlled action toggles fail.
oracles.acceptedDiagnosis: The component render path intentionally throws; the relevant component/boundary and application source should be identifiable where Vue/browser evidence exposes it.
oracles.honestyRequirement: Component file metadata/source attribution is not business-cause proof beyond the observed throw path.
oracles.verificationExpectation: Error-count replay can be meaningful after an explicit fix.

oracles.truth: A watcher on tick schedules another tick change through queueMicrotask until a bounded count is reached.
oracles.acceptedDiagnosis: A watcher-driven reactive feedback chain causes repeated updates; exact dependency/business causality may remain unavailable to the current Vue adapter.
oracles.honestyRequirement: Repeated lifecycle/update observations must not be labeled as exact reactive dependency causality.
oracles.verificationExpectation: Update-count reduction can verify an intervention, but automatic root-cause proof is not expected.

oracles.truth: VueFaultLabRenderStormProbe updates value eight times on a 10 ms interval.
oracles.acceptedDiagnosis: A short intentional update burst exceeds the default update-budget pattern; inspect whether the update frequency is intentional before changing code.
oracles.honestyRequirement: The budget signal is correlation/threshold evidence. The tool must not call high-frequency updates inherently wrong.
oracles.verificationExpectation: Owner-scoped update count is a meaningful before/after target if the same burst workflow is replayed.

oracles.truth: LitFaultLab._networkFailure invokes fetch('/api/fail') and the server returns an intentional HTTP 503.
oracles.acceptedDiagnosis: The application invocation source for the failing request is useful; the HTTP 503 itself may originate server-side.
oracles.honestyRequirement: Invocation provenance must not be presented as the cause of the server failure.
oracles.verificationExpectation: A successful-response/error-count target can be useful after an actual server/client fix, but this pilot need not manufacture one.

oracles.truth: LitFaultLab._runtimeError queues an intentional error unless the existing Fixed error mode is enabled.
oracles.acceptedDiagnosis: The runtime error path is directly reproducible and has a predefined fixed-mode replay.
oracles.honestyRequirement: A successful replay verifies error-count improvement but remains correlation-level unless separate governed causal evidence exists.
oracles.verificationExpectation: The existing Finding -> Verify Fix path should support an owner-scoped runtime-error count without inventing causality.

oracles.truth: _leakListener registers anonymous resize listeners that retain arrays and never records them through governed resource ownership.
oracles.acceptedDiagnosis: The application leaks listeners, but exact ownership/retainer proof is not available from ordinary Level 0 evidence in the current Lit path.
oracles.honestyRequirement: Level 0 must not claim a confirmed resource-lifetime violation for an untracked listener. Targeted governed resource evidence may make the lifetime visible.
oracles.verificationExpectation: Unsupported automatic verification is acceptable until explicit resource evidence/target exists.
